result.markdown: --- gd-head-tags: - >- ``{=html} open-graph: title: >- [Graph.list_triangles()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Edgecase description: List all triangles in the graph. twitter-card: title: >- [Graph.list_triangles()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Edgecase description: List all triangles in the graph. title: >- [Graph.list_triangles()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 bread-crumbs: false toc-depth: 3 description-meta: List all triangles in the graph. page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} List all triangles in the graph. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L32578-L32630){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature Graph.list_triangles() ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![List triangles](/assets/graphs/list-triangles.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="A six-node graph with two triangles, 3, 5, 6 in the accent color and 2, 4, 5 in teal, sharing node 5, plus a four-node cycle 1, 2, 5, 3 that is not a triangle. The card lists the two triangles in matching colors, (3, 5, 6) and (2, 4, 5)." width="100%"} Returns a list of all triangles (3-cycles) in the graph. Each triangle is represented as a sorted tuple of three node IDs. For undirected graphs, each triangle appears once. For directed graphs, lists directed triangles. Time complexity: `O(m * d_max)` where `m` is edges and `d_max` is maximum degree. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [list[tuple[int, int, int]]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : List of triangles, where each triangle is a tuple of three node IDs. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} Each triangle is reported as a tuple of its three node IDs -- here, two triangles both sharing the "A"-"B" edge: ::: {#94a43245 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_nodes(["A", "B", "C", "D"]) .add_edges([("A", "B"), ("B", "C"), ("C", "A"), # One triangle ("A", "D"), ("D", "B")]) # Another triangle ) triangles = graph.list_triangles() [tuple(graph.get_label_from_id(nid) for nid in tri) for tri in triangles] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` [('A', 'B', 'C'), ('A', 'B', 'D')] ``` ::: ::: This makes it straightforward to identify every triadic closure in a larger network -- for example, listing all mutual-friend groups in a small social graph: ::: {#b19f3275 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_nodes(["Alice", "Bob", "Charlie", "David"]) .add_edges([("Alice", "Bob"), ("Bob", "Charlie"), ("Charlie", "Alice"), ("Alice", "David"), ("David", "Bob")]) ) [tuple(graph.get_label_from_id(nid) for nid in tri) for tri in graph.list_triangles()] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` [('Alice', 'Bob', 'Charlie'), ('Alice', 'Bob', 'David')] ``` ::: :::
